purpose: This medicine is used to treat a rare and serious blood clotting disorder called acquired thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, or aTTP. It works alongside plasma exchange therapy and other treatments to help prevent dangerous blood clots from forming in your small blood vessels. It can help reduce the risk of serious complications and death from this condition.
how_it_works: Your blood contains a protein called von Willebrand factor, which normally helps control bleeding. In aTTP, this protein causes tiny clots to form in your blood vessels, which can be very dangerous. Caplacizumab works by blocking this protein so it cannot cause those harmful clots to form, giving your body a chance to recover.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is bleeding, which can show up as nosebleeds, bleeding gums, bruising more easily than usual, or bleeding at the injection site. You may also notice headache or tiredness. Some patients have minor skin reactions where the medicine is injected.
warnings: Because this medicine affects clotting, it increases your risk of bleeding. Tell your doctor right away if you have any unusual or severe bleeding, including blood in your urine or stool, or coughing up blood. Your doctor may need to temporarily stop this medicine before any surgery or invasive procedures. Do not stop taking it on your own without talking to your doctor first, as stopping too soon can be very dangerous.
typical_dosing: The first dose is given by your healthcare team as an injection into a vein before your first plasma exchange treatment. After that, you give yourself one injection under the skin each day, typically in the belly area, every morning before your plasma exchange session. You continue the daily injections for 30 days after your last plasma exchange. Your doctor will tell you exactly how long to keep taking it based on how you are doing.
